clue.text: The one that ended in disaster was the first to leave the band

definitions.text: The one that ended in disaster

indicators.note: the words for being first depart from the name of the band, taking themselves off the front

parts.note: Led Zeppelin, the British rock group
to be first is to have LED the way

explanation.surface: A musician who quit a group first, and whose story ended badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hindenburg airship burned at Lakehurst in 1937; strip the word meaning 'was first' from the rock band's name to leave the airship.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindenburg was a rigid German airship of this type, famously destroyed by fire.

clue.text: Spoil line inserted in software program

indicators.note: the line letter is put into the middle of the program word

parts.note: a bot is an automated software program

explanation.surface: A coder complains that adding a line to a program ruined it.
explanation.definitionFit: To blot something is to stain or mar it, as in blotting one's copybook.

clue.text: Commodity box not popular with central Greece

indicators.note: the popular word is not there, so it comes out of the box word

parts.note: a coffin is a wooden box for burial
IN means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: only the middle letters of the country name are kept

parts.note: its centre gives EE

explanation.surface: A trader describes a shipping crate unpopular in the heart of Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee is a traded agricultural good, one of the world's major soft commodities.

clue.text: Land matter disheartened revolutionary

parts.note: to count is to matter, as in 'every vote counts'

indicators.note: the heart of the word is removed, keeping only its outer letters

parts.note: its first and last letters give RY

explanation.surface: A dispirited rebel feels land matters little any more.
explanation.definitionFit: A country is a nation or territory, one sense of land.

clue.text: Small pasty-faced bulb developer

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly-looking

explanation.surface: A pale little gardener who breeds bulbs.
explanation.walkthrough: The bulb is the electric light bulb, not a garden one: Joseph Swan developed an incandescent lamp alongside Edison.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Joseph Swan was the English inventor who developed the incandescent electric lamp.

clue.text: It provocatively reveals band drinks last of moonshine

parts.note: a strip is a narrow band
teas are cups of tea

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: ends in E

explanation.surface: A band is caught on a moonshine-fuelled drinking session that turns revealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A striptease is a performance in which clothes are slowly removed to expose the body.

clue.text: Type of music sung in French or Albanian

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning their junction

parts.note: the letters run across 'French or Albanian'

explanation.surface: A kind of song performed in either French or Albanian.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral music is written for a choir to perform with voices.

clue.text: Rolling in it as the result of my agitation

parts.note: 'My!' and 'Well!' are both exclamations of surprise
a to-do is a fuss or commotion

explanation.surface: Someone claims they got rich by getting worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my agitation' reads as one phrase, but it is two pieces: the exclamation and the fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rolling in it is an idiom for being very wealthy, which is what well-to-do describes.

clue.text: Police team taking top off chain guard

indicators.note: the first letter of the police unit is removed

parts.note: SWAT is an armed police unit

explanation.surface: An armed police unit beheads a chain guard.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the abbreviation for chain, the old unit of length.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep watch is to guard, and a watch is also a guard or sentry.

clue.text: Mark wastes comeback

indicators.note: the slang word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to top someone is slang for kill, as is waste

explanation.surface: A sports report on a scoring mark wasted by a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small mark or stain on a surface.

clue.text: Provided inverted crannies designed for gnomes?

indicators.note: the conditional word is turned the other way round

parts.note: 'provided' means 'if', as in 'provided it rains'

indicators.note: the letters are arranged into a new design

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Upside-down nooks have been built for garden gnomes.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'gnomes of Zurich' is a phrase for Swiss bankers, so the gnomes are not garden ornaments.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnomes is a disparaging nickname for international bankers and money men, after the gnomes of Zurich.

clue.text: Place associated with fever epidemic

parts.note: ague is a malarial fever with shivering

explanation.surface: A town linked with a fever outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is a deadly infectious disease spreading widely, an epidemic.

clue.text: It brings relief to a minor reptile that's swallowed abandoned wiper

definitions.text: It brings relief to a minor

indicators.note: the reptile word takes the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: gater is a variant spelling of gator, an alligator

indicators.note: abandoned means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run loose

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A small reptile has gulped down a discarded windscreen wiper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a minor reptile' wants to be read together, but the minor is a baby and belongs to the definition. Gripe water is a British remedy for babies' colic.
explanation.definitionFit: Gripe water is a medicine given to infants to soothe colic and wind.

clue.text: Alight one more time on bench

parts.note: RE means 'about' or 'on the subject of'
a settle is a wooden bench with a high back

explanation.surface: A bird lands once again on a bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To alight is to settle, so doing it again is to settle anew.

clue.text: Large liquid expanse of hydrogen discharged from small African tree

indicators.note: the hydrogen symbol is let out of the tree word

parts.note: the shea is a West African tree yielding shea butter

explanation.surface: Hydrogen leaks from an African tree into a great body of water.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea is a large body of salt water, smaller than an ocean.

clue.text: Mouthy thing elected Conservative — is nothing right?

parts.note: someone voted in is IN
taken as written
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A loud-mouthed Tory has been elected; can nothing be right?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouthy' suggests a loudmouth, but here it just means found in the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: An incisor is a front cutting tooth, literally a thing of the mouth.

clue.text: See 26
One tree in the French island

indicators.note: the tree phrase sits between the two letters of the French article

parts.note: la is the French feminine 'the'
A is the indefinite article, meaning one
a palm is a tropical tree

explanation.surface: A single tree grows on a French island.
explanation.definitionFit: La Palma is one of the Canary Islands, a Spanish volcanic isle.

clue.text: Presented a rear view across a river that's cut off

indicators.note: the bare backside stretches across, holding the other letters inside it

parts.note: to moon is to show one's bare buttocks
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bared their bottom across a river from those stranded.
explanation.definitionFit: Marooned means stranded or isolated, left cut off from others.

clue.text: Fan of Slough confined by a physician!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the swamp word is held inside the doctor letters

parts.note: DR is the title abbreviation for doctor, a physician
a slough is a swamp, as is a mire

explanation.surface: A fan from the English town of Slough is locked up by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: Capitalised, Slough looks like the Berkshire town near London; it is the swamp sense.
explanation.definitionFit: An admirer is an enthusiast or devotee, someone who is a fan.

clue.text: Fancy decaff tea — not one that's pretentious

indicators.note: fancy as a verb hints at fanciful rearrangement of these letters
the letter for one is left out of the fodder

parts.note: anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A snob orders decaffeinated tea, then thinks better of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like an invitation to want decaff tea; it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Affected behaviour is artificial and showy, designed to impress, i.e. pretentious.

clue.text: New one, perhaps, needs backing of the others

indicators.note: the little word 'of' is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
the rest means the others

explanation.surface: A newcomer needs support from everyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The New Forest is a national park in Hampshire, England, so 'New one' is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Forest is an ancient woodland area in southern England.

clue.text: Fruit makes pop star extremely randy

parts.note: Cher, the American singer

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of the word are taken

parts.note: gives RY

explanation.surface: A tabloid line: fruit puts a pop diva in an amorous mood.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherry is a small round stone fruit.

clue.text: Don't start deliberately to sink a marine creature!

indicators.note: the first letter of the sinking word is dropped

parts.note: to scuttle a ship is to sink it on purpose

explanation.surface: A plea not to drown a sea creature on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuttle is short for cuttlefish, a squid-like sea mollusc.

clue.text: Intermission. It's not good for a server

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a point at which there is a break or pause

definitions.text: It's not good for a server
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in tennis, a point that would let the receiver win the server's game

explanation.walkthrough: The server sounds like a waiter or a computer; it is the tennis player serving.
explanation.definitionFit: A break point in tennis threatens the serving player's game, and generally means a place to pause.

clue.text: Police finally after father who released a bull

indicators.note: the father word comes first, followed by the police letter

parts.note: pop is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: ends in E

explanation.surface: A dad who set a bull loose arrives after the police.
explanation.walkthrough: A bull here is a papal bull, a formal decree, not an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pontiff issues edicts called papal bulls, named for their lead seal.

clue.text: Mere game?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a mere is a lake or pond
second meaning: a cue sport played on a table

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' looks like the adjective meaning 'only'; it is the noun for a small lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is a small body of water, like a mere, and also a cue game like billiards.

clue.text: Action on the pitch made public swoon

parts.note: a pass is a ball played to a teammate in football
something out is revealed or published

explanation.surface: A footballer's move is exposed, and someone faints.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass out is to faint or lose consciousness, as one does in a swoon.

clue.text: Odious ultimately servile character, one lacking initiative

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: ends in S
Uriah Heep, the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A hateful toady with no get-up-and-go.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep is a person who follows the crowd without thinking for themselves.

clue.text: Tip when carrying table: middle of leg is joined

indicators.note: the tip word holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: the end of something is its tip
a list is a table of items

indicators.note: the centre letter of the short word is taken

parts.note: its middle letter is E

explanation.surface: Moving furniture: the table tips, and a leg comes loose at the joint.
explanation.definitionFit: To have enlisted is to have signed up for or joined the armed forces.
